issues.description: Constructor Developer.init: The problem statement and template expect an initializer with signature init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?). The template defines init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) (template file), and the problem description instructs initializing those two properties and calling swiftExperienceDescription() in the initializer. However, the solution implementation declares init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?, age: Int) (adds an extra 'age' parameter), while the solution's Client calls Developer(...) with only the two parameters (name and monthsOfSwiftExperience). This mismatch between the solution's Developer initializer and both the template/problem statement (and between the solution's initializer and its own Client usage) will cause a compilation error and confuses students about the intended constructor signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the Developer initializer signature across all artifacts. Remove the extraneous 'age: Int' parameter from solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Developer.swift so the initializer matches the problem statement and template: change to init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) and inside the initializer set self.name and self.monthsOfSwiftExperience and call print(self.swiftExperienceDescription()). Alternatively, if the 'age' parameter is intentionally required, update the problem statement, template, and all client usages to include and document the new 'age: Int' parameter consistently.

issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for the Developer concept: the problem statement (and the template) require an initializer init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?), but the solution repository defines a different initializer init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?, age: Int). The solution's Client then calls Developer(...) with only the two parameters (name, monthsOfSwiftExperience), creating an inconsistency between the required API (problem + template) and the solution implementation. Students will be unsure which initializer signature to implement and may be blocked by a compile-time mismatch or confusion about whether an additional 'age' parameter is required.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Developer initializer consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: remove the extraneous 'age' parameter from the solution's initializer so it becomes init(name: String, monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) and update the solution file accordingly. Alternatively (less preferred), update the problem statement, template, and all call sites (Client) to require and document the additional 'age: Int' parameter. Ensure the initializer signature is identical in the problem statement, template, solution implementation, and usage sites.
